events.title: Perl 1.0 released
events.summary: Larry Wall posted Perl 1.0 to comp.sources.misc on December 18, 1987 — a language for text processing and systems glue.
events.about: Perl excels at chewing through text: log files, CSV exports, HTML scraping, and one-off sysadmin scripts. Its regex syntax and `$_` default variable became legendary. Before Python dominated DevOps, Perl powered early web (CGI), bioinformatics pipelines, and Unix automation — many `awk`/`sed` one-liners grew into full Perl programs.

narrative.whyChosen: Perl was the duct tape of the early web and Unix era — practical text manipulation with C-like power.
narrative.whyImportant: It influenced PHP, Ruby, and JavaScript regex culture; CPAN showed how a language could ship a massive reusable library ecosystem.
narrative.problemSolved: Wall needed something better than shell, awk, and sed for report generation at Unisys — one language for parsing, printing, and gluing Unix tools.
